business_summary: Apple designs and sells premium consumer hardware (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Watch, AirPods) and attaches a high-margin, recurring Services business (App Store, iCloud, Apple Music/TV+, AppleCare, advertising, search-licensing, payments) to the installed base. In fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended 2026-06-27) revenue was $109.417B, of which iPhone $54.252B (49.6%) and Services $30.739B (28.1%). The business model is: sell a device at a ~35-40% hardware margin, then earn a software-like recurring cut from the same customer for years. FY2026 has seen a sharp re-acceleration: 9-month revenue $364.357B, +16.2% vs $313.695B a year earlier, driven by the iPhone 17 cycle, Mac, and Services. UPDATE 2026-10-24: no new financial filing since the Q3 FY2026 10-Q - fiscal Q4 2026 (quarter ended ~2026-09-26) results will be released 2026-11-02, so all fundamentals below still reflect the period ended 2026-06-27. Leadership changed on 2026-09-01: John Ternus (formerly SVP Hardware Engineering) became CEO and Tim Cook became Executive Chairman. The iPhone 18 Pro launched at $1,199 (+$100 vs iPhone 17 Pro) and the $1,999 iPhone Duo foldable went on sale 2026-10-23, as Apple passes rising memory costs to customers.

moat.type: Ecosystem switching costs + premium brand + installed-base network effect + extreme capital efficiency and silicon vertical integration

quality.revenue_growth_3y: ~6.8% CAGR from FY2023 ($383.285B) to TTM ended 2026-06-27 ($466.823B); most recent year +16.2% (9M FY2026 $364.357B vs 9M FY2025 $313.695B) - a sharp re-acceleration off a flat 2022-2024 base
quality.gross_margin: 48.7% TTM (gross profit $227.14B on revenue $466.823B, = Q4 FY2025 $48.341B + 9M FY2026 $178.8B); 50.1% in Q3 FY2026 but that included ~2pp of one-off tariff-refund benefit; company guided 47-48% for Q4 FY2026
quality.roic: ~67% TTM. NOPAT ~$127.6B (TTM operating income $154.83B x (1 - 17.6% effective tax rate)) over invested capital of ~$191.8B (shareholders' equity $107.5B + total term debt and commercial paper $84.3B). Excluding the $146.5B of cash and marketable securities the return on operating capital is far higher.
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: negative - Apple is NET CASH by ~$62.2B ($146.517B cash + marketable securities vs $84.3B term debt + commercial paper at 2026-06-27). Ratio is not meaningful; balance-sheet risk is effectively nil.
quality.fcf_positive: yes; TTM free cash flow ~$136.7B (TTM operating cash flow $146.72B less capex $10.04B). 9M FY2026 alone: OCF $116.996B - capex $6.799B = $110.20B.

valuation.verdict: expensive - trading ~49% above our base fair value and ~26% above the high end of the band
valuation.method: UNCHANGED inputs (no new filing since 2026-09-17, so per the playbook the fair value is NOT moved). Blend of two methods via code/valuation.py. (1) P/E: TTM diluted EPS $8.73 (Q4 FY2025 $1.85 + 9M FY2026 $6.88) x 24 / 28 / 33. 28x base = Apple's 10-year median P/E (~27.25x); 33x high allows for the growth re-acceleration; 24x low for a 3.75-4.00% Fed funds rate. (2) FCF yield: TTM FCF per diluted share $9.29 ($136.683B / 14.715B diluted shares) at required yields of 5.0% / 4.2% / 3.5%. At $347.69 the stock trades at 39.8x TTM EPS and a 2.67% TTM FCF yield. FORWARD CROSS-CHECK (aggregator, not used in the band): consensus FY2027 EPS ~$9.58 (24/7 Wall St., 2026-10-06) x 24/28/33 = $229.92/$268.24/$316.14 - even on next year's estimated earnings at our high multiple the price is ~10% above the high end; at $347.69 the stock is ~36.3x forward EPS.
valuation.trend: Price $347.69 (2026-10-23 close) is above its 50-day average ($329.49) and well above its 200-day average ($294.39); 52-week close range $246.72-$348.34 on Alpaca daily closes - trading at/near an all-time closing high. Strong uptrend; momentum, not value, is supporting the price. Sell-side consensus target (~$328 mean / $340 median, 44 analysts) sits BELOW the price.

bull_case: Wide moat proven by pricing power: company gross margin reached 50.1% in Q3 FY2026 and 48.7% TTM - extraordinary for a business that is still ~74% hardware by revenue (TTM Products $346.3B of $466.8B).
Growth genuinely re-accelerated: 9M FY2026 revenue +16.2% YoY and 9M diluted EPS +22.4% ($6.88 vs $5.62), with iPhone +21.7% and Greater China +22.4% in Q3 FY2026 - the China-decline narrative broke.
Services is a $120.5B-TTM annuity (Q4 FY2025 $28.750B + 9M FY2026 $91.728B) growing ~14% and carrying much higher margins than hardware; it converts one-time device sales into recurring cash.

Fortress balance sheet: ~$62.2B net cash. No refinancing risk, and a $100B buyback authorization added 2026-04-30 on top of $38.0B remaining - $62.1B of stock repurchased in 9M FY2026 alone, shrinking diluted shares ~2%/yr (15,056M in Q2 FY2025 to 14,726M in Q2 FY2026).

Cash generation is enormous and capital-light: $136.7B TTM FCF on only ~$10B of capex - Apple gets AI compute largely through partners (Google Gemini powers the revamped Siri) rather than tens of billions of its own capex, unlike its mega-cap peers.

New CEO is the hardware chief: John Ternus (Apple since 2001, led iPhone/Mac/iPad hardware engineering) took over 2026-09-01 in a planned, board-unanimous succession, with Tim Cook staying on as Executive Chairman - continuity rather than disruption.

Pricing power is being exercised: iPhone 18 Pro launched at $1,199 (+$100, ~9%) and 1TB models +$300, and a $1,999 foldable (iPhone Duo) adds a new top price tier - the brand can pass through cost inflation.
risks: VALUATION IS THE THESIS-KILLER. At $347.69 the stock is 39.8x TTM EPS and a 2.67% TTM FCF yield, against a 10-year median P/E of ~27.25x. Our base fair value is $232.82; the price is ~49% above it, and ~26% above our optimistic high case ($276.76). Even on consensus FY2027 EPS (~$9.58) at 33x the value is ~$316. The sell-side mean target (~$328) is below the price too. There is no margin of safety; there is a large negative one.

Peak-earnings risk on top of peak-multiple risk. Q3 FY2026's 50.1% gross margin included ~2 percentage points (and $0.11 of EPS) of one-off tariff refunds following the February 2026 Supreme Court ruling. Guidance for Q4 FY2026 is 47-48% gross margin and 9-11% revenue growth - a clear deceleration from 16%. Buying 38x earnings that are themselves flattered is how permanent capital loss happens.

MEMORY-COST SQUEEZE is now the dominant margin risk. Management called memory pricing a '100-year flood' on the 2026-07-30 call and said memory costs more than explained the sequential gross-margin decline guided for Q4 FY2026; ex-tariff-refund gross margin already fell from 49.3% (March qtr) to 48.1% (June qtr) and the Q4 guide midpoint ex-refunds is ~46.5%. TrendForce estimated 256GB memory cost up nearly 400% YoY. Price hikes may not fully offset, and they risk dampening unit demand (reports of iPhone 18 Pro order cuts are unconfirmed).

Cost and supply squeeze ahead. The Q3 FY2026 10-Q warns of 'supply constraints and increasing costs for components' and expects those trends 'to intensify' - advanced-node (2nm/3nm) capacity and rising memory prices. Management also flagged a ~2.5pp FX headwind to Q4 growth.

Regulatory attack on the highest-margin revenue. (a) EU DMA: a EUR 500M fine already levied and a separate Article 6(4) investigation that could carry penalties of up to 10% of worldwide net sales. (b) Epic: the Ninth Circuit's December 2025 injunction barring any commission on purchases made outside an app remains; the Supreme Court granted review of the civil-contempt standard on 2026-06-30. (c) DOJ's March 2024 monopolization suit. (d) Remedies in the Google search case could cut Apple's search-licensing revenue, which is near-100%-margin.

iPhone concentration and cycle dependence: ~50% of revenue from one product. The current 16% growth is substantially an upgrade-supercycle effect; supercycles pull demand forward and create brutal comparisons the following year.

AI dependence has been outsourced. Apple's revamped Siri runs on Google's Gemini models. That fixed the near-term product gap, but it means Apple is renting rather than owning the most important platform technology of the decade, and it deepens a commercial relationship that regulators are actively attacking.
Greater China remains ~17% of revenue ($18.816B of $109.417B in Q3 FY2026) and a large share of manufacturing - a standing geopolitical and tariff exposure.

Leadership transition: a new CEO (Ternus, from 2026-09-01) has not yet delivered a single quarterly report as CEO; the first is 2026-11-02. Execution, capital-allocation and AI-strategy choices could change.

Sentiment is stretched: analysts are trimming, not raising, in aggregate - Loop Capital cut to Hold ($370 to $330), MoffettNathanson cut to $283 (Neutral), Morgan Stanley trimmed to $355; consensus FY2027 EPS slipped from $9.68 to $9.58 over three months. Earnings estimates are drifting down while the price makes new highs.
what_would_break_thesis: Company-wide gross margin falls below 44% for two consecutive quarters (it is 48.7% TTM; guidance is 47-48%).
Q4 FY2026 (reported 2026-11-02) or Q1 FY2027 gross margin excluding tariff refunds falls below 45%, or management guides below 45% - evidence that memory costs are overwhelming pricing power.
Total revenue shrinks year-over-year for two consecutive fiscal years.
Services revenue declines year-over-year for two consecutive quarters (Services is the moat's cash register).
iPhone revenue declines year-over-year for three consecutive quarters, indicating the upgrade franchise - not just a cycle - has broken.
The net cash position of ~$62.2B turns into net debt of more than 1.0x EBITDA.
TTM free cash flow falls below $90B (a ~35% drop from the current $136.7B).

A final, non-appealable regulatory or court outcome that forces Apple to give up its App Store commission on a material share of transactions, or that ends the Google search-licensing payments, without an offsetting replacement.
Annual buybacks fall below $40B while the balance sheet still holds net cash - a signal management no longer believes the shares are worth retiring.
Any serious accounting red flag, restatement, or auditor change.
PRICE DISCIPLINE (entry rule, not a sell rule): do not initiate or add above $233 (base fair value). A first tranche is only justified below ~$205 (base less our 12% minimum margin of safety).
catalysts: Q4 FY2026 results on 2026-11-02 (first report under CEO Ternus): checks the 9-11% revenue guide (~$111.7-113.7B; consensus ~$113.3B / EPS ~$1.99) and the 47-48% gross-margin guide, plus December-quarter guidance on memory costs. THIS THESIS MUST BE RE-REFRESHED IMMEDIATELY AFTER 2026-11-02 regardless of refresh_due.
A pullback into the $200-$233 zone - the only thing that would make this ownable. Requires a ~33-42% decline from $347.69.
iPhone 18 / iPhone Duo foldable sell-through and Gemini-powered Siri with iOS 27 - if AI features drive upgrades, high growth could persist.
Supreme Court outcome in the Epic contempt matter, or the Google-search-remedy ruling - could re-rate Services either way.
Further memory-price inflation or easing - the single biggest swing factor for FY2027 gross margin.
